title: Compile JSX by hand
prompt:
JSX is function calls. The starter gives you `h(type, props, ...children)`, a simplified version of what the compiler produces. Complete `buildCard(movie)` so it returns exactly what this JSX would create: ```jsx

{movie.title}

{movie.year}

``` Use the `movie` argument, not hard-coded values.
hints: The first argument is the tag name as a string, the second is the props object (or `null`), and every argument after that is a child.
Attributes go in the props object: `{ className: 'card' }`.
Children can be other `h()` calls: `h('article', { className: 'card' }, h('h2', null, movie.title), …)`.
explanation: Each JSX tag becomes one call: the tag name, then an object of attributes, then the children in order. Curly-brace expressions like `{movie.title}` are just arguments, which is why only expressions are allowed inside them. React's real `jsx()` differs in details (it receives children already inside the props object instead of as extra arguments, a single child isn't wrapped in an array, and keys are passed separately), but the tree of plain objects is the same idea.

checks.root: The root is an "article" with className "card"
checks.two-children: It has two children: an "h2" then a "p"
checks.title-text: The h2 contains the movie title
checks.uses-data: It works for any movie, not only Arrival
